findings.title: Hung flusher processes are never killed before replacement
findings.body: In production, processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, producing SpawnProcess objects. SpawnProcess is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context process class on Linux), so isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is false and process.kill() is never called. _create_process_for_shards then starts a replacement for the same shards while the hung original remains alive; both can call flush_segments and produce for the same Redis shards, causing duplicate segment production and leaked processes. The check should use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or exclude threading.Thread instead.

findings.title: join() can return without terminating all flusher processes
findings.body: join() waits for processes sequentially against a shared deadline. If the deadline expires while waiting for an early process, the loop breaks and never calls terminate() on the remaining processes. The terminate() call that is reached is also guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which is false for SpawnProcess objects created through the spawn context. A process hung in flushing or producing can therefore survive join() and continue running alongside a new flusher after rebalance, risking duplicate flushes. Daemon status does not help because the parent consumer process remains alive across rebalances.

findings.title: Invalid flusher process counts are not validated
findings.body: max_processes is accepted without requiring a positive value. An explicit 0 is treated by 'max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)' as unset and unexpectedly spawns one process per shard, while a negative value makes num_processes negative, creates an empty process_to_shards_map, and then fails with an opaque KeyError when shards are assigned. Since --flusher-processes accepts any integer in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py, operators can trigger either excessive process creation or a consumer startup crash instead of a clear configuration error. Validate the value at the CLI and/or SpanFlusher boundary.

findings.title: Comma-joined shard metric tag corrupts per-shard metrics for shared processes
findings.body: shard_tag is built by joining multiple shard IDs with commas and then used as a single metric tag value. This is the common case when one flusher process handles several shards, including the CLI default of one process. In StatsD-style tag encoding, commas separate tags, so a value such as '0,1,2' is parsed as shard:0 plus stray tags rather than one shard dimension, making the produce and segment-size metrics unusable for per-shard analysis. The wait_produce timer at line 199 also inconsistently names the tag 'shards' instead of 'shard'. Emit metrics per shard or use a sanitized single-value grouping tag consistently.

findings.title: New multiprocess test never exercises spawning or actual multi-shard flushing
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit passes produce_to_pipe, which forces SpanFlusher to use threading.Thread instead of the production spawn-process path, and it only asserts process counts and shard-map totals without submitting or flushing any spans. Consequently the tests do not cover spawn pickling of per-shard SpansBuffer objects, run_with_initialized_sentry argument handling, per-process Kafka production, shared-process flushing for multiple shards, or process kill/restart behavior. A regression in the production multiprocess path could pass while the consumer duplicates or loses flushed segments.
